9293               	;
9294               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
9295               	; 	'
9296               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
9297               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
9298               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
9299               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
9300               	; 	'
9301               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
9302               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
9303               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
9304               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9305               	; 	'
9306               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
9307               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
9308               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
9309               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
9310               	; 	'
9311               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
9312               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
9313               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
9314               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
9315               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for
9316               	; 	' a genuine stall and at five it only fires for one.

9797               cv593
9798               	;
9799               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9800               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9801               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9802               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9803               	; 	' runs every pass.
9804               	; 	'
9805               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9806               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9807               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9808               	; 	'
9809               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9810               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9811               	; 	'
9812               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9813               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9814               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without

9930               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9931               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9932               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9933               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9934               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9935               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9936               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9937               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9938               	; 	'
9939               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9940               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9941               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9942               	; 	'
9943               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9944               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9945               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9946               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9947               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9948               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9949               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9950               	; 	'
9951               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9952               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9953               	; 	'
9954               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9955               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9956               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9957               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9958               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9959               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9960               	; 	'
9961               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the

9964               	; 	' before any of this.
9965               	; 	'
9966               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9967               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9968               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the

10412               	;
10413               	; 	' ======================================================================
10414               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10415               	; 	' ======================================================================
10416               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10417               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10418               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10419               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10420               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10421               	; 	'
10422               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10423               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10424               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10425               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10426               	; 	' broken.
10427               	; 	'
10428               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10429               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10430               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10431               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10432               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10433               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10434               	; 	'
10435               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10436               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10437               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10438               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10439               	; coll_obst:
10440               cvb_COLL_OBST

     E2A6 219A     
10761               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10762               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10763               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10764               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10765               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10766               	; 	' away from.
10767               	; 	'
10768               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10769               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10770               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10771               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10772               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10773               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10774               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10775               	; 	'
10776               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10777               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10778               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10779               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10780               	; 	'
10781               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10782               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10783               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10784               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10785               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10786               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10787               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10788               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10789               	; 	'
10790               	; 	' A ducking Kop is still stood up, because the crouch is a held pose and
10791               	; 	' there is nothing to interrupt.

10950               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
10951               	; 	'
10952               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
10953               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
10954               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
10955               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
10956               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
10957               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
10958               	; 	'
10959               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
10960               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
10961               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
10962               	; 	'
10963               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
10964               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
10965               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
10966               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
10967               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
10968               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
10969               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

11075               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.

11079               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11080               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11081               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11082               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11083               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had

12220               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12221               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12222               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.

12226               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one

12255               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12256               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12257               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12258               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12259               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12260               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12261               	; 	'
12262               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12263               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12264               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12265               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12266               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12267               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12268               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12284               	; 	' that cross a floor -- and groups them WEST then EAST, because only one
12285               	; 	' direction is ever on screen: screen 0 carries a west flight and screen
12286               	; 	' 7 an east one.

12289               	; 	' `define_char`, which in bitmap mode is LDIRVM3 -- the TRIPLE copy, once
12290               	; 	' per screen third. It therefore costs three times what the character
12291               	; 	' count suggests, which is why these screens run slower than the rest.
12292               	; 	'
12293               	; 	' THE WEST SCREEN USED TO COST HALF AS MUCH AGAIN, because it carries TWO
12294               	; 	' flights: floor 1's crosses into a shop floor and floor 3's into the
12295               	; 	' roof, so it needed both composite sets -- nine characters against the
12296               	; 	' east's six, 216 bytes a pass against 144. It measured 20 passes a

12565               	;
12566               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12567               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12568               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12569               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12570               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12571               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12572               	; 	'
12573               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12574               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12575               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12576               	; 	'
12577               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12578               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12579               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12580               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12581               	; 	'
12582               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12583               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12584               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12585               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12586               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12587               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12588               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12589               	; 	'
12590               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12591               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12592               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12593               	; 	'
12594               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12595               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why
12596               	; 	' scan_escs and scan_elev redraw every tick rather than once.
12597               	; scan_furn:
12598               cvb_SCAN_FURN

12939               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
12940               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12941               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12942               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12943               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12944               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
12945               	; scan_wipe:
12946               cvb_SCAN_WIPE
12947               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12948               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12949               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12950               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12951               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12952               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12953               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12954               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12955               	; 	'
12956               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12957               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12958               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12959               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12960               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12961               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12962               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12963               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12964               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12965               	; 	'
12966               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12967               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12968               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12969               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12970               	; 	'
12971               	; 	' renumber.py rewrites this line from genart.SCAN_FIRST, and
12972               	; 	' checkstruct.py fails the build if the two disagree.

13042               	; 	' THE TWO ACTORS ARE SPRITES; EVERYTHING ELSE IS CHARACTERS.

13044               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
13045               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
13046               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
13047               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
13048               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the
13049               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
13050               	; 	'

13052               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers
13053               	; 	' merged and the blink was the only thing left to tell them apart. Two
13054               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.
13055               	; 	'
13056               	; 	' The furniture is drawn ONCE, by scan_furn. It used to be redrawn every
13057               	; 	' tick because erasing a character-based marker ANDed bits out of
13058               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
13059               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.
13060               	; 	' -- the lift car. IT WAS FLICKERING, and the cause was not the drawing
13061               	; 	' but the ERASING: scan_elev cleared its three cells and put them back
13062               	; 	' every tick, whether or not the car had moved, so several times a second

13850               	;
13851               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13852               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13853               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13854               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13855               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13856               	; 	'
13857               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13858               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13859               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13860               	; 	'
13861               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13862               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13863               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13864               	; 	'
13865               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13866               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13867               	; 	'
13868               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13869               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13870               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13871               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13872               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13873               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13874               	; 	'
13875               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13876               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13877               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13878               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13879               	; 	'
13880               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13881               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13882               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13883               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)

14000               	;
14001               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14002               	; 	'
14003               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14004               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14005               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14006               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14007               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14008               	; 	'
14009               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14010               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14011               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14012               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14013               	; 	' counting stops.
14014               	;
14015               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
14016               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
14017               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
14018               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
14019               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
14020               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
14021               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
14022               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
14023               	; 	'
14024               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
14025               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
14026               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).

14181               	;
14182               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay
14183               	; 	' counters are not ticked inside this loop -- a tone still sounding when
14184               	; 	' the pause starts would hang for its whole duration, which is the classic
14185               	; 	' CVBasic sticky-audio failure.
14186               	; 	' EVERY CHANNEL OFF, AND THE DECAY COUNTERS WITH THEM. The counters are
14187               	; 	' ticked by the main loop, so anything still sounding when the loop stops
14188               	; 	' -- for a capture, a death, the bonus count -- sustains for as long as
14189               	; 	' whatever replaced the loop takes. That is where the long beep over the
14190               	; 	' bonus tally came from: not the tally's own note, which turns itself off
14191               	; 	' after every unit, but a footstep or a hit that was still ringing when
14192               	; 	' Harry was caught.
14193               	; snd_off:
14194               cvb_SND_OFF
14195               	; 	' EVERY CHANNEL sfx_tick CAN WRITE, AND CHANNEL 3 IS ONE OF THEM. This
14196               	; 	' routine was written when the footstep was a pair of tones on channel 0
14197               	; 	' and it still named only 0, 1 and 2 after the footstep moved to the
14198               	; 	' NOISE channel. So a step ringing when Harry was caught was never turned
14199               	; 	' off: it hissed through the whole bonus tally and did not stop until the
14200               	; 	' next round's first footstep happened to reset it.
14201               	; 	'
14202               	; 	' Zeroing sot does NOT silence it. The counter only emits its note-off on
14203               	; 	' the pass it reaches zero, so setting it to zero by hand skips the very

14629               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14630               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14631               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14632               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14633               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14634               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14635               	;
14636               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14637               	; 	'
14638               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14639               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14640               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14641               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14642               	; 	'
14643               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14644               	; 	'
14645               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14646               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14647               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14648               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14649               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14650               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14651               	; 	'
14652               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14653               	; 	'
14654               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14655               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14656               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14657               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14658               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14659               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14660               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14661               	; 	'
14662               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14663               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14664               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14665               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14666               	; 	'
14667               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14668               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14669               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14670               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14671               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14672               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14673               	; 	'
14674               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14675               	; 	'
14676               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14677               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14678               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14679               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14680               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14681               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not

14806               	;
14807               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14808               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14809               	; 	'
14810               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14811               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14812               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14813               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14814               	; 	'
14815               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14816               	; 	'
14817               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14818               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14819               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14820               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14821               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14822               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14823               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14824               	; 	'
14825               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14826               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14827               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14828               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14829               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14830               	; 	'
14831               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14832               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14833               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14834               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14835               	; 	#if TI994A
14836               	; 	BANK 2
14837      010C     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15501               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15502               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15503               	; 	'
15504               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15505               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15506               	; 	' being small sprites.
15507               	; 	'
15508               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15509               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15510               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15511               	; 	'
15512               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15513               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15514               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15515               	;
15516               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15517               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16646               	;
16647               	; 	' -------------------------------------------------- scanner canvas
16648               	; 	' Chars 208-255: 16 cols x 3 rows over screen rows 21-23. Blank to start;
16649               	; 	' dots are plotted by VPOKEing the PATTERN table (rows 21-23 sit in the
16650               	; 	' third screen third, so every scanner pattern is at base 4096).
16651               	;
16652               	; 	' --------------------------------------------------- font colours
16653               	; 	' Chars 32-90, EIGHT bytes each. Without this the font keeps whatever
16654               	; 	' CVBasic left in the colour table, which on a green store made the HUD
16655               	; 	' unreadable.
16656               	;
16657               	; scan_col3:	' one 8-byte block per canvas row: 4 px of GREY margin, then a 3 px band of furniture GREY and a yellow floor line, per 4 px level, on dark green. The Kop and the crook are coloured PER CHARACTER at run time -- see scan_set
16658               cvb_SCAN_COL3

16773               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16774               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16775               	; 	'
16776               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16777               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16778               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16779               	; 	'
16780               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16781               	; 	' blit is
16782               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16783               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16784               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16785               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16786               	; 	'
16787               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16788               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16789               	; 	'
16790               	; 	' template ids:
16791               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16792               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16793               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16794               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16795               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16796               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16797               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16798               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16799               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16800               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16801               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16802               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16803               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16804               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16805               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
